description: A three-panel composite of secondary-electron images (SEI, 15.0 kV, instrument tagged NTUST) of a Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C austenitic steel after isothermal holding at 700 °C; every panel carries a scale bar and a magnification. (a) ×20,000 with a 1 µm bar: an austenite grain boundary outlined by a chain of bright, blocky second-phase particles, with a very fine, dense needle-like/lamellar texture filling the matrix on both sides. (b) ×10,000 with a 1 µm bar: an advancing cellular colony growing from a boundary into the matrix, its lamellae annotated γ, α and κ — bright κ lamellae alternating with dark α plates inside γ. (c) ×2,000 with a 10 µm bar: a low-magnification overview in which coarse, several-µm-long lamellar colonies of different orientations fill a wedge/triangular region and impinge on the surrounding unreacted grains. Read together, the three panels document the same cellular transformation at increasing time and decreasing magnification: bright second-phase particles nucleate on austenite grain boundaries (a), develop into a lamellar (γ + κ + α) colony (b), and coarsen into large interpenetrating colonies (c). No numeric data values are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: All three panels are secondary-electron (SEI) images acquired at 15.0 kV, with the instrument label 'NTUST' printed in the lower-right of each panel.
Panel (a) is recorded at ×20,000 with a 1 µm scale bar; panel (b) at ×10,000 with a 1 µm scale bar; panel (c) at ×2,000 with a 10 µm scale bar.
In (a) a grain boundary is decorated by a chain of bright blocky particles, while both adjoining grains carry a very fine, dense lamellar/needle-like textural relief.
Panel (b) shows lamellae explicitly labelled with the phase symbols γ, α and κ, the bright lamellae being marked κ and the darker ones α.

Panel (c) shows coarse lamellar colonies of several different orientations filling a large wedge-shaped region and impinging on surrounding unreacted grains at a much lower magnification (×2,000, 10 µm bar).

The caption states the panels correspond to isothermal holding at 700 °C for (a) 1 h, (b) 25 h and (d) 100 h, but the supplied images are labelled (a), (b) and (c); the caption's '(d) 100 h' does not match the visible (c) panel label.

The caption states the figure shows the growing feature of κ-carbides in the austenite and the evolution of the κ*-carbide in (κ + γ + α) lamellar colonies on the austenitic grain boundaries (caption OCR renders these as 'j0-carbides' and 'j*-carbide').
The caption identifies the material as a Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C austenitic steel [122].

The citing text states that the lamellae of (α + γ + κ) develop initially from the austenite grain boundaries as lamellar colonies and grow from the grain boundaries via the cellular transformation in this Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C steel.

The citing text describes the cellular transformation as a discontinuous precipitation reaction γ → γ + κ + α (or γ → γ + κ + α + M23C6) in which κ and α nucleate simultaneously at grain boundaries and grow into the austenite as nodules of lamellar mixture.
The citing text also notes that lamellar κ-carbide grains are always accompanied by austenite twins in the lamellar austenite grains.
No numeric composition, hardness, or phase-fraction values are printed anywhere in the three panels; only magnification, accelerating voltage, scale bar and the instrument label appear.

subfigures.description: SEI micrograph, ×20,000, 1 µm scale bar, 15.0 kV, NTUST. A single austenite grain boundary marked by a chain of bright blocky particles; both adjacent grains show a dense, very fine lamellar/needle-like relief texture with scattered bright precipitates.

SEI micrograph, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar, 15.0 kV, NTUST. A lamellar cellular colony growing into the austenite; individual lamellae are labelled γ, α (dark) and κ (bright), with κ lamellae alternating with α plates. Labels are small but legible.

SEI micrograph, ×2,000, 10 µm scale bar, 15.0 kV, NTUST. Lower-magnification overview of coarse lamellar colonies with several different orientations filling a wedge-shaped region and meeting unreacted grain interiors; individual plates are on the order of µm in length.

caption OCR garbles the phase symbols as 'j0-carbides' and 'j*-carbide' (presumably κ-carbide and κ*-carbide) and renders subscripts/superscripts inconsistently
